headline: Denmark's crown prince says he is open to deployment
deck: Christian, now a platoon leader in the Royal Life Guards, says he was very unsure about joining the armed forces at first.
standard: Crown Prince Christian, heir to the Danish throne, is open to staying in the military after he qualifies as a lieutenant, and would 'definitely find it interesting' to be deployed, he told Politiken. He did not say where.
He became a second lieutenant this summer and is now a platoon leader in the Royal Life Guards, an infantry regiment of the Danish army, helping to train conscripts.

He doubted his choice when he began conscription in February 2025: 'On the drive down there I was shaking all over,' he said. In the interview he also spoke for the first time about press interest in videos of him at a music festival this summer.
short: Crown Prince Christian, heir to the Danish throne, would 'definitely find it interesting' to be deployed once he qualifies as a lieutenant, he told Politiken.

definitions.definition: an infantry regiment of the Danish army
